memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And rejoice before the Lord your God at the place he will choose as a dwelling for his Name—you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, the Levites in your towns, and the foreigners, the fatherless and the widows living among you. Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and follow carefully these decrees. - Deut 16:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the wide circle of joy God draws. He calls the family to rejoice, but also the servants, the Levites, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. No one is left standing outside. God's joy was never meant to be a private party for the comfortable few. It reached to those most easily forgotten.

And God gives a reason, "Remember that you were slaves in Egypt." Their past bondage was meant to soften their hearts toward the vulnerable. A people who had been rescued should never look down on the powerless. Grace received should overflow as grace shared.

This is God's heart, and it shines even more brightly in Christ. He welcomes the outsider, lifts the lowly, and forms a family where the servant and the foreigner sit at the same table (Gal 3:28). When we remember that we too were once slaves to sin and were set free by pure mercy, we cannot hold others at arm's length. Our joy grows fuller precisely when we include those the world overlooks. Who is on the edges of your life that God might be calling you to draw into the circle of His joy?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who tends to be left out of your circle of joy?
2. How does remembering your own rescue change how you treat others?
3. What is one way you can include a forgotten person this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for welcoming me when I was an outsider. Widen my heart to include those the world forgets. Amen.
